livingworld.config.title: Living World
livingworld.config.subtitle: environment settings
livingworld.option.enabled.tooltip: Master switch for every visual and audio effect. Turning it off returns the game to vanilla rendering without restarting.
livingworld.option.effectIntensity.toolt: Scales the amount of environmental particles across all systems. Lower it for a subtler world, raise it for a more dramatic one.
livingworld.option.biomeAmbience.tooltip: Each biome's own airborne life: pollen, fireflies, blowing sand, spindrift, cave drips, embers, End motes.
livingworld.option.temperatureHud.toolti: Displays the temperature your character feels in the corner of the screen.
livingworld.option.itemPhysics: Dropped items lie on the ground
livingworld.option.itemPhysics.tooltip: Dropped items tumble while they fly and come to rest lying flat (blocks on a face, stacks in a pile) instead of hovering and spinning. They rock on water and flutter in strong wind. Only how they are drawn changes; pick-up and everything the server knows are untouched.
livingworld.option.heatHaze.tooltip: Rippling air over hot ground. Strongest at midday toward the horizon, gone in shade, rain and at night. Needs the atmosphere pass.
livingworld.option.heatHazeStrength.tool: How strongly hot air distorts the distance.
livingworld.option.coldBreath.tooltip: You and other players exhale visible vapour in cold air, faster when sprinting.
livingworld.option.temperatureTint.toolt: A gentle warm cast in scorching heat and a cool cast in freezing cold.
livingworld.option.dustDevils.tooltip: Small whirlwinds that wander across hot, dry ground on calm afternoons.
livingworld.option.seasons.tooltip: The year turns through spring, summer, autumn and winter: summers run hot, winters cold, winter showers fall as snow and cold ground keeps a covering of it. Follows the world's day counter; a server running the mod sets the length of a season.
livingworld.option.seasonalFoliage.toolt: Leaves and grass change with the season: fresh green in spring, gold and red in autumn, brown and bare-looking in winter. Evergreens stay green. Not active with Sodium or a shader pack.
livingworld.option.seasonHud.tooltip: A small calendar in the top-left corner: the season, the day within it, and a bar of the whole year with a mark at today.
livingworld.option.temperatureEffects.to: Optional gameplay: extreme heat and cold drain hunger faster and can slow you slightly. Never deals damage. Off by default; all visuals work without it.
livingworld.option.temperatureEffects.lo: This rule is controlled by the server you are playing on (config/livingworld-server.json).
livingworld.option.customPrecipitation.t: Replaces the vanilla rain and snow sheets with individual streaks and flakes that slant and surge with the wind and stop at roofs and canopies.
livingworld.option.rainDensity.tooltip: Number of rain streaks drawn, within the budget of the graphics preset.
livingworld.option.rainSplashes.tooltip: Material-aware splashes where rain lands, ripples on water, and drips from wet leaves during and after rain.
livingworld.option.wetSurfaces.tooltip: Ground the rain can reach darkens as it gets wet and dries out afterwards. Needs the atmosphere pass (Balanced preset or higher).
livingworld.option.puddles.tooltip: Reflective puddles collect on exposed ground in prolonged rain, ripple while it falls and evaporate later. Purely visual: no blocks are changed.
livingworld.option.stormClouds.tooltip: When volumetric clouds are off: a moving layer of cloud closes over the sky as weather builds, darkens in storms and is lit from within by lightning.
livingworld.option.thunderDelay.tooltip: Thunder arrives after the flash according to how far away the strike was, quieter and duller with distance.
livingworld.option.distantLightning.tool: Occasional sheet lightning beyond the horizon during thunderstorms, followed by a far-off rumble.
livingworld.option.lightningFlash.toolti: How strongly lightning lights up the screen. See also Accessibility > Reduce flashes.
livingworld.option.snowDensity.tooltip: Number of snowflakes drawn, within the budget of the graphics preset.
livingworld.option.blizzards.tooltip: Allows snowfall to intensify into wind-driven whiteouts that cut visibility. Off caps snowfall at a gentle level.
livingworld.option.snowCover.tooltip: While it snows, exposed surfaces gradually whiten, then clear after the storm. Purely visual. Needs the atmosphere pass.
livingworld.option.iceCrystals.tooltip: Glittering diamond dust drifting in very cold, still air.
livingworld.option.sandstorms.tooltip: When strong wind sweeps dry, dusty biomes the air fills with blowing sand and visibility drops.
livingworld.option.sandstormFrequency.to: How readily wind whips up a sandstorm. 0 disables naturally occurring ones.
livingworld.option.sandDensity.tooltip: Amount of sand streaking past during a sandstorm.
livingworld.option.blowingSand.tooltip: Streams of sand and dust skimming over dry ground whenever the wind picks up, even without a full storm.
livingworld.option.footprints.tooltip: Players and creatures leave blocky, pixel-art prints in sand, snow, mud and soft ground, on the same texel grid as the block textures. Wind, rain and snowfall wear them away texel by texel. Purely visual.
livingworld.option.footprintLifetime.too: Multiplier on how long prints last in calm, dry weather.
livingworld.option.mobFootprints.tooltip: Animals and monsters leave their own kinds of tracks: hooves, paws, bird feet, heavy round prints.
livingworld.option.wetFootprints.tooltip: Coming out of water or in from the rain, you leave damp prints on hard floors that fade as your feet dry.
livingworld.option.stepParticles.tooltip: Steps and landings throw up what the ground is made of: sand grains, powder snow, mud, dust, grass, puddle splashes.
livingworld.option.litFootprints.tooltip: Shades each texel of a print against the real sun and moon direction, so its darker and lighter edges change through the day. Off uses a simpler pre-shaded print.
livingworld.option.vegetationSway.toolti: Grass, flowers, crops, vines and leaves move with the wind field. Uses the vanilla terrain shaders: not available with Sodium, and shader packs do their own.
livingworld.option.swayStrength.tooltip: How far vegetation moves in the wind.
livingworld.option.vegetationBending.too: Grass and flowers are pushed aside as you move through them.
livingworld.option.fallingLeaves.tooltip: Leaves detach from trees, flutter down and rest on the ground for a while. More fall when it is windy.
livingworld.option.windStrength.tooltip: Multiplier on the wind you experience. Affects everything wind touches: rain slant, particles, sound, erosion of footprints.
livingworld.option.atmosphericFog.toolti: Humidity haze, dust, rain mist and storm whiteouts, each contributing its own colour and density.
livingworld.option.fogDensity.tooltip: Multiplier on all fog added by the mod.
livingworld.option.groundMist.tooltip: Low-lying mist at dawn, over swamps, after warm rain and in damp caves. Needs the atmosphere pass.
livingworld.option.colorGrading.tooltip: Subtle climate-dependent colour response: warm deserts, cool mountains, muted storms, golden sunsets.
livingworld.option.gradingStrength.toolt: How pronounced the colour grading is.
livingworld.option.exposureAdaptation.to: Stepping out of a cave is briefly dazzling; stepping in is briefly dark until your eyes adjust.
livingworld.option.lightShafts.tooltip: Soft rays where the low sun breaks through trees and mist. Ultra and Cinematic presets only.
livingworld.option.volumetricClouds.tool: Replaces the game's flat clouds with a layer of real, three-dimensional cloud that is lit by the sun, drifts with the wind, thickens before rain and towers in a storm. Balanced preset and up; costs frame rate on weak graphics chips.
livingworld.option.cloudShadows.tooltip: The shadows of the clouds drift across the land. Needs volumetric clouds.
livingworld.option.enhancedSky.tooltip: A deeper blue overhead, a glowing horizon, fuller sunrise and sunset colours, a night sky crowded with twinkling stars and the Milky Way, and rainbows when the sun comes out on wet air.
livingworld.option.aurora.tooltip: On some clear, cold nights curtains of green and violet light move across the sky. Needs the enhanced sky.
livingworld.option.waterRipples.tooltip: Rings spread from raindrops and from anything moving through water.
livingworld.option.entitySplashes.toolti: Creatures entering or racing through water throw up droplets and spray.
livingworld.option.wetDrips.tooltip: Water runs off players and creatures for a few seconds after they leave the water.
livingworld.option.waterMist.tooltip: Sea spray on windy shores, spray at the foot of waterfalls and mist over very cold water.
livingworld.option.waterShading.tooltip: Water you can see through: the bed is refracted by the ripples and fades to blue-green with depth, the surface mirrors the sky and glitters under the sun or moon, rain rings it and it fades softly into the shore. Works with the vanilla renderer; with Sodium or a shader pack, water keeps the look they give it.
livingworld.option.waterReflections.tool: The water mirrors the terrain, trees and builds around it (traced in screen space, so only what is on screen can be mirrored). Off, or on the Performance preset, it mirrors the sky only.
livingworld.option.waveHeight.tooltip: How rough the water is. Still air leaves it nearly smooth with slow ripples; wind raises waves that run downwind, so a storm is always rougher than a calm day.
livingworld.option.caustics.tooltip: The moving web of light that ripples focus onto the bed, seen through the water from above and all around you when you dive.
livingworld.option.shoreline.tooltip: Where water meets land: foam along the edge, bands of surf that run in toward the shore and grow with the wind, and sand that lies dark and damp along the waterline.
livingworld.option.ambience.tooltip: A continuously synthesised soundscape of wind, rain, wildlife and caves that follows the weather and your surroundings. Uses the Ambient and Weather volume sliders.
livingworld.option.ambienceVolume.toolti: Level of wind, wildlife, caves and other ambience (on top of the game's Ambient/Environment slider).
livingworld.option.weatherVolume.tooltip: Level of rain, snowfall and thunder (on top of the game's Weather slider).
livingworld.option.wildlife.tooltip: Birdsong by day, crickets and frogs by night, insects in the heat, surf on the coast.
livingworld.option.recordedWildlife.tool: If a resource pack provides recordings for the mod's bird and frog sound events, play those in place of the synthesised calls. Without such a pack this changes nothing.
livingworld.option.caveEcho.tooltip: Nearby sounds return a short echo when you are deep underground.
livingworld.option.replaceVanillaRain.to: Use the mod's surface-aware rain instead of the vanilla rain loop. Turn off to hear both the vanilla loop and the new ambience.
livingworld.option.shiver.tooltip: A slight tremble of the view, in bursts, when you are bitterly cold.
livingworld.option.heatSway.tooltip: A slow, heavy drift of the view in punishing heat.
livingworld.option.windBuffet.tooltip: Strong gusts nudge the view when you stand exposed to them.
livingworld.option.cameraEffects.tooltip: Scales all camera movement added by the mod. Every effect stays under one degree even at maximum.
livingworld.option.frostOverlay.tooltip: Ice crystals creep in from the screen edges in extreme cold and melt as you warm up.
livingworld.option.lensDroplets.tooltip: Droplets bead on the view after surfacing from water or when you look up into heavy rain.
livingworld.option.preset.tooltip: Hard budgets for particles, precipitation and footprints. Performance: essentials only. Balanced: full weather, footprints, wet ground. Ultra: denser, plus light shafts. Cinematic: maximum, for screenshots and high-end systems.
livingworld.option.particleDensity.toolt: Scales spawn rates within the preset's budget.
livingworld.option.adaptiveQuality.toolt: When the frame rate falls below the target, particle and precipitation counts are reduced smoothly, and restored when there is headroom.
livingworld.option.targetFps.tooltip: The frame rate adaptive quality tries to protect.
livingworld.option.effectDistance.toolti: Radius around you in which footprints, splashes and local particles are simulated.
livingworld.option.bloom.tooltip: Torches, lava, the sun, lightning and glitter on water bleed softly into what is around them. Stronger in the dark, restrained in daylight. Balanced preset or higher.
livingworld.option.bloomStrength.tooltip: How far and how brightly light sources glow.
livingworld.option.sunGlow.tooltip: A warm halo in the sky around the sun (strongest when it is low) and a faint cool one around the moon, hidden by overcast.
livingworld.option.filmLook.tooltip: A gentle film-style response: muted colours gain a little life, highlights roll off instead of clipping, mid-tones gain contrast, shadows lean cool and highlights warm. 0 leaves colours exactly as the game draws them.
livingworld.option.vignette.tooltip: Slightly darkens the corners of the view. Drawn under the hand and the HUD, never over them.
livingworld.option.postProcessing.toolti: The full-screen pass that provides heat shimmer, mist, wet ground, puddles, cloud deck, eye adaptation and grading. Disable it if another mod's post-processing conflicts; essential fog still works through vanilla fog.
livingworld.option.yieldToShaderPacks.to: While an Iris shader pack is active, switch to simple rendering and skip the atmosphere pass so the pack stays in charge of lighting and post-processing.
livingworld.option.simpleRendering.toolt: Draw everything with the game's stock shaders only. Use this if you see rendering glitches with an unusual mod combination.
livingworld.option.overrideSkyColors.too: Lets sandstorms and blizzards colour the sky and clouds. Turn off if another sky mod should have the final say.
livingworld.option.reduceCameraMotion.to: Removes all camera movement added by the mod (shivering, heat sway, wind buffeting).
livingworld.option.reduceFlashes.tooltip: Limits lightning flashes to a faint glow.
livingworld.option.reduceDistortion.tool: Removes heat shimmer and softens the refraction of water on the lens.
livingworld.option.reduceFog.tooltip: Keeps storms, mist and haze light enough that you can always see at least 72 blocks.
livingworld.option.reduceParticles.toolt: Cuts environmental particles to about a third.
livingworld.option.screenOverlays.toolti: Frost, lens droplets and temperature vignettes drawn over the view. Turn off for a completely clear screen.
